Aug 27 Heatmap Atlas

Per-condition heatmaps of block darkening over time: three magnet repeats against their three controls, one condition per panel. Gap (injection) side is on the left of every cell, magnet side on the right.

How to read: each panel is one condition; left column = the three magnet repeats, right column = their three controls. Every cell is a position–time heatmap: horizontal axis is distance from the injection gap (0–10 mm, magnet side at right), time runs downward (0–21.5 h, linear), color is local darkening vs the same block at t = 0 (each frame’s overall level removed first, so block-wide drift is suppressed). White ticks on the left edge mark actual photo times; the field is smoothly interpolated between them. One shared color scale (0–55 L*). Telling transport from structure: genuine transport grows and spreads as time descends — a wedge widening from the gap side. Features that sit at a fixed position with fixed width from the very first frames are structure, not particles: thin vertical stripes are gel wrinkles, and the zone right of the dashed line (~8.5 mm) is the gel–case seam plus, in magnet cells, the magnet’s shadow — its brightness flickers with lighting but it never spreads. Nothing can genuinely arrive at 9 mm within the first hour. The wall-arrival and band-depth analyses are on the companion figures page.
